topics.title: What Station is
topics.summary: Station is a local-first agent workspace where agent work is run, observed, and evidence-gated, so "done" is a gate verdict rather than the agent's own confidence.

topics.title: These docs, and what they cannot do
topics.summary: station-docs is a read-only documentation server: an engine that has it can EXPLAIN Station but CANNOT operate it — operating Station needs the separate station-control server, which only some engines can receive.
topics.section: These docs, and what they cannot do

topics.title: Projects
topics.summary: A Project organizes durable work, layouts, Agents, knowledge, and settings, with explicit resource and workspace bindings where needed.

topics.title: Agents and engines
topics.summary: An agent is the actor you pick to do work; an engine is what actually executes it — Station's own engine or an external engine such as Claude Code, Codex, or a custom CLI engine you connect by its command.

topics.title: Connections
topics.summary: Connections separates Model connections used by Station's engine from external Engines that run their own loop.

topics.title: The built-in assistant, and what it needs
topics.summary: The built-in assistant is the agent that operates Station for you; it needs the station-control tool server, which only engines with a reviewed delivery mechanism can receive.
topics.section: The built-in assistant, and what it needs

topics.title: Sessions, turns, and runs
topics.summary: A session is one bounded episode of agent work, a turn is one user-to-agent interaction inside it, and a run is the tracked execution accounting for that work.

topics.title: Tasks and the task workspace
topics.summary: A task is a durable work identity owned by a project — it outlives any single session, keeps its workspace binding and references, and can be reopened after a restart.

topics.title: Scheduled jobs and notifications
topics.summary: A scheduled job runs an agent on a cron schedule and produces runs like any other work; notifications are contributed by subsystems and plugins and aggregated by Station.

topics.title: Skills
topics.summary: A skill is a reusable bundle of instructions and behavior an agent adopts; skills are a Station-agent capability, and only engines with a skills channel receive them.

topics.title: MCP tool servers, integrations, and tools
topics.summary: An integration is an MCP server that exposes tools; a tool is one callable within it, and Station ships two built-in servers — station-control (operate Station) and station-docs (explain Station).
topics.section: MCP tool servers, integrations, and tools

topics.title: Trust, gates, evidence, and receipts
topics.summary: Station renders evidence-gated process state — Flow gates and verdicts, Veritas readiness, Surface trust bundles — beside the work, and never computes those verdicts itself.

topics.title: Fleet inference across Stations
topics.summary: Fleet inference lets one Station serve model capacity to another Station you control, with routing and serving receipts — and contribution is opt-in and off by default.

topics.title: Plugins and the registry
topics.summary: Plugins extend Station through published contracts, declared contributions, and admitted capabilities such as layouts, Agents, tools, providers, and knowledge namespaces.

topics.title: Writing a plugin: manifest, Workspace Panes, SDK hooks, validation and install
topics.summary: How to write a Station plugin that adds a Workspace Pane: the Agent Plugins 1.0 manifest with its io.kontourai.station extension, the components export, the SDK hooks a pane can call, how to check it with validate_plugin, and how a person installs it.
topics.section: Writing a plugin: manifest, Workspace Panes, SDK hooks, validation and install

topics.title: Station vocabulary
topics.summary: A compact glossary of the words Station uses precisely: Station, device, engine, agent, project, task, session, run, gate, evidence, receipt, and the retired term "runtime".
